column1: # Phiogy's looks: a look's name, and after it a row that changes the
# theme for that look, written as data/theme.tsv writes one. The first
# is the one Phiogy opens in. A look with nothing to change is the theme
# as it is. What each is called is data/text.tsv's: look.<name>.
# A look changes the ground, the inks and how much light there is; the
# light itself stays one colour, and there is enough of it in every look
# for a ground at rest to be seen (`shade.share`), and no more: the
# grounds group things and are to be very subtle (the user, 23 November
# 2026). Every icon, row, message and part stands on one in every look. The two glass looks are Apple's Liquid
# Glass as Phiber wears it (phiber: theme/style/glass.rs): the window's
# ground lets the desktop show, blurred by the system (window.glass), and
# the window's panes, its bar and a panel that floats, blur what is
# behind them inside it (glass.*). Buttons, rows and icons are not glass.
# Glass opens first: it is the default (the user, 25 November 2026).
# In the dark looks the light is faint, so what is chosen or on is lit
# three and a half times the share (`shade.strong`): it reads as chosen.
# Glass with nothing open keeps its own grey ground; only a modal's veil
# darkens the window (the user, 25 November 2026: "darkness not needed
# here", after it was made as dark as the veil). A dark look's ground is
# whole, never see-through: what shows through it (a light desktop) would
# make the ground lighter than what stands on it (the user, the same day).
# Its panes are still glass, blurring the window inside it.
# The Liquid Glass looks are Apple's as its own apps wear it (the
# Landmarks sample, BOT-anist's panels): clearer glass than the others,
# bending more at its rim and catching more light there, every part on
# a pane of it, and every corner rounder, the parts' and the modals'
# most of all. Its edge is a shine, thin and nearly the glass's own
# colour, not a border. Its text stands a point off the glass, a light
# under it (`text.shade`, `text.lift`), as on Vision Pro's panes.
# The plain looks are the ordinary ones, as Apple's own apps on a Mac
# stand: a grey ground with white grounds on it, and a faint hairline down
# the sidebar's edge toward the page (activity.line, activity.rim).
# Silver (the user, 25 November 2026, from a stainless fridge door and
# its dispenser): brushed steel grounds with more light on them than
# the others, as the steel takes it, and a black ink as the recess
# has. The light falls as on the white lunch box and the yellow tub
# shown beside it: soft, from above, each ridge of a ground catching it.
# Sixteen glass looks, as Apple Vision Pro and Meta Horizon wear glass
# (the user, the same day): each is Liquid Glass, light or dark, with
# its own tint, how much it blurs and colours what is behind it, how
# much of it shows, how far its rim bends light, and how bright its
# edge is. A light tint lets the desktop show through the window; a
# dark one keeps its ground whole (dark grounds are never lighter).
# Vision, Thin and Thick are visionOS window glass; Horizon is Meta's.
